supplement.holds: The external SI contains the detailed design/materials (Section A and Fig. S1), examples (B1.3), evaluation details (B3.1, B3.2, B4.1), Study 1 comparisons (Tables S1-S2), Study 2 demographics/balance (S3-S4), email-quality regressions (S5), interrater reliability (S6), prompt-length robustness (S7-S8), email-length analysis (S9), time (S10), confidence/difficulty (S11-S12), and task-type interactions (S13), as referenced on pp. 2-6. The full regression tables and their numerical uncertainty are absent from this PDF. The supplement itself could not be retrieved, so its numerical contents were not independently inspected.

paper_design_summary: Study 1 had trained evaluators rate 600 GPT-4-generated business recommendations across English, Arabic, and Chinese; it does not compare AI-generated and human-generated work (p. 2, Methods). Study 2 reports a sample of 480 people randomly assigned to write business emails with supplied AI recommendations or without AI assistance, with evaluators scoring Creativity, Completeness, Relevance, and Actionability and the analysis also measuring output length (pp. 2-3, Methods and Statistical analysis; p. 6, productivity results).

studies.label: Study 1: evaluation of AI-generated business recommendations

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people were assigned to AI assistance. GPT-4 responses to business prompts were evaluated across English, Arabic, and Chinese (p. 2, Methods).
assignment.quote: ChatGPT-4 was then used to generate responses to each prompt in all three languages, resulting in 600 AI-generated responses (200 prompts

participants.who: The production sample consists of 600 AI-generated responses to 200 business prompts in three languages. Six native-speaker evaluators, two per language, had relevant business-domain experience; they are raters, not people producing creative work or receiving AI assistance (p. 2, Methods).
participants.quote: a team of six native speakers (two for each language) with prior experience in the relevant business domains were recruited.

ai_tool.how_used: Generated business recommendations in English, Arabic, and Chinese for evaluation; no human-authored comparison outputs (p. 2, Methods).

task.description: AI responses to common business issues in marketing, customer service, human resources, and R&D were rated for Completeness, Relevance, Actionability, and Creativity (p. 2, Methods).

studies.label: Study 2: randomized business-email writing with or without AI-generated recommendations

assignment.what_was_assigned: Individuals were randomly assigned to receive a pregenerated AI response below the email-task instructions or to write without AI-generated assistance. Language groups are observed groups, not randomized language assignments. The experiment is clearly randomized, but the main PDF does not identify an online panel, a supervised laboratory, or an ordinary-work/coursework setting; design_class is other pending the external design description (p. 2, Methods; p. 9, Limitations).
assignment.quote: The participants were randomly assigned to either a treatment group, wherein they were provided with AI-generated content to assist their writing of an email to address a hypothetical business issue;
assignment.locator: p. 2, Methods, Study 2 paragraph; p. 2, Research motivation and overview
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 3, Methods continuation: https://osf.io/u7s2g; the registration itself was not inspected

arms.name: AI-generated content
arms.description: Pregenerated ChatGPT-4 business recommendations were presented as text directly under the task instruction and could assist the email. The paper reports 240 treated participants across the three languages (p. 2, Research motivation and overview).

arms.name: Control without AI-generated content
arms.description: Write the business email as in a typical work setting, without using AI-generated content. The paper reports 240 participants in this group across the three languages (p. 2, Research motivation and overview; Methods).

participants.exclusions: The reported study sample is 480 people, including 240 with AI-generated content and 240 without (p. 2, overview and Methods). The sample includes responses passing the attention check and taking more than the suggested time, stated as: "The sample includes all responses that passed the attention check and in which participants took more than the 15-minute suggested time." (p. 3, Methods continuation). The original assignment/recruitment total and the number excluded are not separately stated, so randomized counts remain null; the reported sample is not labeled intention-to-treat.
participants.who: People proficient in English, Arabic, or Chinese; 160 in each language setting (p. 2, Methods). The main PDF does not name a recruitment platform or establish that the sample consists of students, online-panel members, professionals, or a general-public sampling frame; population is left null. Per-language treatment/control counts are not printed and were not inferred by dividing the language totals.
participants.country: Countries not stated. Participants are described as spread across the world (p. 9, Limitations). Language is not treated as country.
participants.quote: Specifically, a preregistered experiment was implemented, which involved 480 human participants (160 per language) proficient in English, Arabic, or Chinese.
participants.locator: p. 2, Research motivation and overview and Methods; p. 3, sample inclusion rule; p. 9, Limitations

ai_tool.how_used: The treatment provided the corresponding pregenerated business response from Study 1 directly below the email-writing instructions. Participants used supplied content while producing the scored email; they did not interact repeatedly with an LLM. Model snapshot, generation settings, and the full instructions are not given in this PDF (p. 2, overview and Methods; p. 9, Limitations).

task.description: Write an email addressing a hypothetical business issue in marketing, customer service, human resources, or R&D. The emails propose solutions/recommendations and are explicitly scored for creativity along with completeness, relevance, and actionability (pp. 2-3, Methods). R&D tasks concern new technologies and products (p. 6, Task types).
task.duration: 15-minute suggested time; the stated analysis inclusion rule requires more than that time (p. 3, Methods continuation). No fixed maximum or later-session assessment is reported.

outcomes.name: Email Creativity
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Six trained evaluators rated the human-written emails (p. 2, Methods). Their qualifications are referred to external SI B4.1 and cannot be confirmed from this PDF; coded human_raters rather than asserting expert status. The main text defines Y_i as the rating of email i, so the unit is coded output; it does not explain whether individual evaluator ratings were averaged or retained separately (p. 3, Statistical analysis). The regression observation count is not printed in the main PDF. The paper states that standard errors in all models were clustered at participant level (p. 3, Statistical analysis). A creative email contains multiple suggestions outside the creative repertoire of the average manager (p. 3, Methods continuation). Creativity is explicitly one of the four primary email-quality outcomes (p. 3, Statistical analysis); primary status in the preregistration itself was not checked. Task-type heterogeneity: the main text reports less creativity in Chinese for R&D relative to the marketing baseline (p = 0.025), referring to external Table S13 (p. 6, Task types). This is a moderation analysis of the same outcome. Prompt-length robustness analyses are discussed with external Tables S7 and S8 (p. 5); ordered-logit models, controls, and demographic/experience heterogeneity analyses are summarized without coefficients (p. 6, Task types). These variants are not separate outcomes.

contrasts.reported: Figure 1(d) shows a higher AI-treatment median than control within each language. No numerical within-language AI-versus-control coefficient, arm mean/SD, SE, confidence interval, or p-value is printed in the main PDF. The relevant regression table is external SI Table S5; no values were estimated from boxplot positions.
contrasts.locator: p. 5, Fig. 1(d), Creativity; p. 3, AI effects on the quality of human work across languages (Study 2), reference to SI Table S5

contrasts.reported: Chinese versus English: "0.49 standard deviations less Creativity (p = 0.016)". This is the difference between language-specific AI treatment effects, not a direct AI-versus-control effect or a comparison of the treated groups alone. The standardizing SD and the coefficient SE are not given in the main text.
contrasts.locator: p. 3, AI effects on the quality of human work across languages (Study 2); external SI Table S5

outcomes.name: Email length (normalized characters)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Output length measured as the number of normalized characters (p. 6, AI effects on productivity across languages). The lexical_overlap vocabulary code is used for this lexical count; it is not an overlap/similarity measure and does not compare different people's outputs. The normalization procedure, per-language arm means/SDs, and regression observation counts are not printed in the main PDF. The statistical-analysis section states that model standard errors are clustered at participant level (p. 3). Task-type heterogeneity reports shorter R&D emails in Arabic and Chinese relative to the marketing baseline (p = 0.037 and 0.020, respectively), referring to external SI Table S13 (p. 6, Task types); this is not a separate outcome.

contrasts.reported: English: "49% increase in email length (631 normalized characters; p = 0.000)". The raw increase and p-value are reported, but no SE, confidence interval, or arm means/SDs are printed in the main PDF.

eligibility.reason: Study 2 explicitly randomly assigns individual people to supplied generative-AI content versus no AI-generated content (p. 2, Methods); it reports 480 people, 160 per language, with 240 in each assistance condition overall (p. 2, overview and Methods). Trained evaluators score the actual emails for Creativity and other quality dimensions, with Creativity explicitly primary (pp. 2-3, Methods and Statistical analysis). AI content is available while the email is produced (p. 2, overview), so these are with_ai outcomes. The randomized experiment setting is not specified sufficiently to choose lab_rct, online_rct, or field_rct; other flags that missing subtype and does not negate the explicitly reported random assignment. Study 1 is model_only and supplies no eligible human-output estimate.

one_line_finding: Among 480 email writers, the AI-assistance effect on creativity was 0.49 standard deviations smaller in Chinese than in English (p = 0.016; sample: p. 2, Methods; interaction: p. 3, Study 2 quality results).
open_questions: Retrieve the external SI to establish the randomized experiment setting/recruitment population and replace Study 2 design_class other with the appropriate RCT subtype; the main PDF establishes random assignment but not its setting.

Confirm the pre-exclusion assignment total, exclusion counts, and treatment/control counts within each language; clarify the inclusion wording that participants took more than the 15-minute suggested time (p. 3).

Inspect SI B4.1, B3.2, and Table S5 for evaluator qualifications, scale anchors, aggregation of evaluator ratings, regression observation counts, within-language AI-versus-control coefficients, SEs, and the SD underlying the printed standardized language interactions.
Inspect SI Table S9 for email-length arm summaries and coefficient SEs, and Table S13 for the exact task-type interaction models. These tables are not in the supplied PDF.
notes: Read the entire supplied markdown, including references and end matter, and extracted all ten PDF pages with PyMuPDF. All numerical entries come from those PDF pages; no effects were computed and no numerical values were estimated from figures. Study 1 is retained as a separate model_only study with no outcome entries because it contains no human production or AI-assisted human work and answers none of the three Atlas questions. The five Study 2 entries include all relevant output scores: the four rated quality dimensions and email length. Time to write, self-reported confidence, and perceived difficulty are omitted because they are not scores of the produced output. There is no diversity or post-withdrawal outcome. No within-language arm count was obtained by arithmetic. Cross-language treatment-effect differences are explicitly labeled other contrasts and must not be extracted as direct ai_vs_bau effects. For length, p_value_only indicates the only printed uncertainty information: raw increases are also preserved in reported, and mean_difference_se is not used because no SE is available. Null population and the other design code preserve absent recruitment/setting information. The data link is printed on p. 9, Data availability; no code link is stated. Supplement access was attempted in memory with Python urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 at the Europe PMC full-text endpoint for PMC12373962 and then the publisher article URL; both failed with WinError 10013 (socket access forbidden). No supplement was read or saved.
